question: Will any country other than the DRC have more than 100 confirmed cases of Bundibugyo ebolavirus during 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: outside the DRC only Uganda (20 confirmed; outbreak declared over Aug/Sep, sources differ) and France (1) have Bundibugyo cases as of late Sep 2026, versus about 8,100 in the DRC. Reference class: large DRC and Central African Ebola outbreaks, where neighbouring countries almost always get fewer than 25 imported or limited cases (2018-20 Uganda: 4; this outbreak Uganda: 20 over 4.5 months and 8,000+ DRC cases). Only West Africa 2014-16 had several countries past 100. Upside risks: spread into Dungu next to South Sudan, a traveller who passed through Rwanda and Uganda, conflict, no vaccine. But with about 3 months left plus reporting lag, a new country would have to start sustained transmission almost immediately and pass 100 confirmed. Market check: no matching market; Polymarket and Kalshi only list 'Ebola pandemic in 2026' (Polymarket reported at about 4-7% in search snippets, market pages not opened), a different contract.
calls.dossier:
- Wikipedia 2026 Central Africa Ebola epidemic (late Sep 2026): DRC 8,116 confirmed / 3,924 deaths; Uganda 20 confirmed / 2 deaths; France 1 confirmed; Germany 2 medevacs, counted in the DRC total per WHO.
- WHO data via search summary (26 Aug 2026): 5,815 confirmed = 5,794 DRC, 20 Uganda, 1 France. By 26 Sep: about 8,088 confirmed, so about 2,270 added in a month, all DRC.
- Uganda (RIVM/Wikipedia): 20 confirmed; 14 infected while travelling in the DRC, 5 local transmission; last patient discharged 16 Jul; WHO declared the Uganda outbreak over (25 Aug per one source, 2 Sep per another).
- WHO DON618 (late Sep 2026): outbreak spread to Bulu HZ (Sud-Ubangi) and Dungu HZ (Haut-Uele, bordering South Sudan); about 78 new confirmed in one reporting interval to 25 Sep.
- 11 Sep 2026: case died in Gwaka, Sud-Ubangi, after travelling from South Kivu through Rwanda and Uganda. No confirmed cases found in Rwanda, Uganda or South Sudan from this.
- Al Jazeera 28 Sep 2026: Africa CDC says cases 'levelled off after a rapid increase' but outbreak 'not under control'; community resistance; no approved vaccine or therapeutic for Bundibugyo; conflict near borders with South Sudan, Uganda, Rwanda.
- Historical: 2018-20 DRC (about 3,470 cases) produced 4 Uganda cases; West Africa 2014-16 had Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone each above 100, while imports elsewhere stayed small (Nigeria 20, Mali 8, US 4, Senegal 1).
- Status quo: no non-DRC country is anywhere near 100 confirmed; highest is Uganda at 20 with the outbreak ended.
- Resolution: resolves off the last WHO AFRO External Situation Report released in 2026, not news reports or Wikipedia; no re-resolution.
- Event window: calendar 2026 (1 Jan -> 31 Dec 2026, cumulative count in last 2026 sitrep); as of 29 Sep about 75% of the year elapsed; outbreak began May 2026.
- Searched and not found: any confirmed Bundibugyo cases in South Sudan, Rwanda or Burundi; any matching prediction market (only 'Ebola pandemic 2026' contracts on Polymarket/Kalshi exist).
calls.reference_class: Neighbouring and non-source countries during large Central African Ebola outbreaks (2018-20 DRC, 2022 Uganda, 2026 so far), plus West Africa 2014-16 as the upside case

calls.reasoning: Base rate: in large Ebola epidemics, secondary countries outside the core rarely exceed 100 confirmed cases (West Africa: only the 3 core countries; Nigeria 20, Mali 8; 2018-20 DRC: Uganda 4). The current Uganda BDBV outbreak peaked at 20 confirmed and WHO declared it over in late August 2026; France has 1 imported case. With about 13 weeks left and no other country reporting cases, getting past 100 would need a new, fast-growing, poorly controlled outbreak recorded in the last WHO sitrep of 2026. The very large DRC epidemic (about 8,100 confirmed, eastern border provinces, conflict, no vaccine) keeps a small tail. No human market found.
calls.dossier:
- Wikipedia 2026 Central Africa Ebola epidemic (as of 26 Sep 2026): DRC 8,116 confirmed / 3,924 deaths; Uganda 20 confirmed / 2 deaths; France 1 confirmed. No other country listed with confirmed cases.
- RIVM / search summary (Sep 2026): WHO declared the Uganda BDBV outbreak over on 25 Aug after 42 days without a new case (Wikipedia gives 28 Jul as the date of the last case). Of Uganda's cases, 14 were infected while travelling in the DRC and 5 through local transmission; 8 were in Kampala.
- ECDC: imported cases were a US citizen evacuated to Germany (May 2026) and a healthcare worker in France (24 Jun 2026).
- Al Jazeera 28 Sep 2026: DRC 8,067 confirmed, CFR 48%; cases 'levelled off after a rapid increase'; Africa CDC says 'not under control'; WHO says 'far from over'. Hotspots are North Kivu (Butembo), Ituri and Tshopo. Conflict near the borders with South Sudan, Uganda and Rwanda is hampering the response. No approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo.
- Al Jazeera 23 May 2026: Africa CDC listed 10 at-risk countries, including Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan and Zambia; none has reported confirmed cases in the sources found.
- Growth: about 5,000 confirmed by 23 Aug and about 8,100 by 26 Sep.
- Base rates: in West Africa 2014-16, only Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone exceeded 100 (Nigeria 20, Mali 8, Senegal 1, US 4, Spain 1, UK 1, Italy 1). In the 2018-20 DRC outbreak (about 3,470 cases), Uganda had 4 and no other country had any. In the 2000 Gulu, Uganda outbreak, a single country had 425 cases, which shows a seeded country can pass 100 within months.
- Status quo: no non-DRC country is above 20; Uganda's outbreak is closed.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the last WHO AFRO External Situation Report released in 2026, not media or Wikipedia counts; confirmed cases only.
- Event window: calendar year 2026 (1 Jan -> 31 Dec 2026, measured by the last 2026 sitrep); as of 29 Sep, about 75% has elapsed.
- Searched for but not found: confirmed cases in South Sudan, Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania, Zambia, CAR or Angola; any prediction market on this event.
calls.reference_class: Secondary (non-epicentre) countries in large Ebola epidemics reaching >100 confirmed cases

calls.reasoning: As of ~28 Sep 2026 the DRC Bundibugyo outbreak has ~8,100 confirmed cases and is still growing (~78 new confirmed per 2 days, mostly Ituri/North Kivu). Outside DRC: Uganda 20 confirmed (outbreak declared over ~late Aug/2 Sep), France 1 imported; no other country has any confirmed case. Reaching >100 confirmed in a new country from zero within ~3 months, and captured in WHO's last 2026 sitrep, requires near-immediate sustained local transmission. Base rate from Ebola history: only West Africa 2014-16 produced >100-case spillover countries; North Kivu 2018-20 (3,470 cases) exported just 4 cases to Uganda. Upward risk: record-size outbreak spreading to Haut-/Bas-Uele bordering South Sudan/CAR with weak surveillance; Africa CDC lists 10 at-risk countries. No matching market (Polymarket 'Ebola pandemic 2026' ~4% is a different contract).

calls.reference_class: Large DRC/East-Central African Ebola outbreaks and whether a neighbouring country reached >100 confirmed cases

calls.reasoning: Outside the DRC, only Uganda (20 confirmed, outbreak declared over Aug/Sep 2026) and France (1) have Bundibugyo cases, against about 8,100 in the DRC. Historically, only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic produced other countries with more than 100 cases; the 2018-20 DRC outbreak exported 4 cases to Uganda. With about 3 months left plus reporting lag, a new country would need to start fast, sustained transmission now and be captured in WHO's last 2026 sitrep. The tail stays open because the DRC epidemic is record-size, has spread to zones bordering South Sudan and CAR, faces conflict, and has no vaccine. No matching human market found.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on every material fact: DRC about 8,100 confirmed; Uganda 20, outbreak declared over; France 1; Germany's cases counted under the DRC; no confirmed cases in any other country; no matching market. The only factual discrepancy is whether Uganda's outbreak was declared over on 25 Aug or 2 Sep, which doesn't affect the outcome and can't be settled without web access. Their 0.03 vs 0.04 is pure judgment about how heavy the tail is. I take 0.03: a jump from 0 to more than 100 confirmed cases, recorded in the final 2026 WHO sitrep within about 13 weeks, is very unlikely given the historical pattern.

disagreements.claim: Date WHO declared the Uganda outbreak over (25 Aug vs 2 Sep 2026)
disagreements.verdict: Unresolved without web access; either date means the outbreak is over, so it doesn't matter here

disagreements.claim: How much tail risk to give a new-country outbreak (3% vs 4%)
disagreements.verdict: Took 3%: very short window, reporting lag, and zero confirmed cases in any candidate country
